artists.biography:
Therapy? are a rock band from Northern Ireland. The band was formed in 1989 by guitarist-vocalist Andy Cairns from Ballyclare and drummer-vocalist Fyfe Ewing. Therapy? recorded their first demo with Cairns filling in on bass guitar. To complete the lineup, the band recruited Larne bassist Michael McKeegan. The band signed with major label A&M Records in 1992, for which they released four albums, most notably Troublegum in 1994 and Infernal Love in 1995. Ewing's departure in early 1996 preceded the arrivals of his replacement Graham Hopkins, and Martin McCarrick on cello and guitar. Neil Cooper replaced Hopkins on drums in 2002. Following the departure of McCarrick in 2004, the band have remained a stable three-piece since.

Therapy? are currently signed to UK independent label Marshall Records. The band has released 15 full-length studio albums and has sold over two million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
Semi-Detached is the seventh studio album by Northern Irish rock band Therapy?, released in March 1998 on A&M Records. Produced by Chris Sheldon, the album marked the band's final release for the label after a lengthy recording process that spanned throughout 1997. The record showcases the band's alternative rock sound within the broader pop/rock landscape, continuing their established style of heavy, guitar-driven compositions.

By 1998, Semi-Detached represented a transitional point in Therapy?'s career, arriving during a period when the band was reassessing its direction following their earlier commercial peaks in the mid-1990s. The album was released in multiple formats, including a standard CD edition and a limited 6x7" boxset, reflecting the band's continued investment in physical media presentation. The 44-minute runtime contains the band's characteristic blend of aggressive instrumentation and melodic sensibilities that had defined their output since their emergence in the late 1980s.

While specific critical reception details are limited in available documentation, the album's release on A&M Records proved significant as the band's final project with the label, signaling an impending change in their recording arrangements. Semi-Detached remains part of Therapy?'s substantial discography, representing their work during the late 1990s alternative rock era when the genre's commercial dominance had begun to wane from its earlier heights.
